# Utility Billing and Assistance Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Utility Billing and Assistance Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 9 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model and keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded files, proposed billing, metering, case, workflow and messaging connectors, and channels; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who builds, tests and later uses the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for billing, metering, case-management, workflow and messaging connections with dedicated references; the synthetic workshop needs none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare service, billing, revenue, assistance and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: GitHub Copilot in VS Code Agent mode, the Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Write-control design | Plan authenticated tools, authorization checks, explicit human approval and audit logging before any write is proposed; the local demo performs none. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Utility service business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Manual review of consumption records, billing policy, assistance criteria and account status for disputes and assistance requests. Agree where manual review slows dispute resolution or yields inconsistent resident outcomes before attributing change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Request | Request type | Systems consulted | Evidence missing | Outcome | Resolved on | Reviewer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Utility service business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Utility service business owner | Approve resident-service scope, rate and program-criteria replacement, escalation and success measures; keep synthetic figures out of results. |
| Authorized utility staff | Retain verification, adjustment, agreement, eligibility and enrollment authority; approve every action with the customer. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any utility connection is approved. |
| Utility data and connection owners | Approve billing, metering, case-management, workflow and messaging access through dedicated, least-privilege connection references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check every locked persona case, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject evidence without a positive anchor or target-agent Draft proof. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route resident decisions to authorized staff. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for resident service are agreed.
- [ ] The business owner records how disputes and assistance requests are reviewed today before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/utility-billing-assistance/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded, with maker access granted, before any build starts.
- [ ] The authenticated staff audience and least-privilege scopes for resident, meter and case data are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/utility-billing-assistance/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/utility-billing-assistance/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/utility-billing-assistance/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/utility-billing-assistance/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Utility Billing Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: utility-billing-assistance-rules-and-controls.md
7. Add knowledge: utility-billing-assistance-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_assistance-programs
9. Add skill: aibast_billing-inquiry
10. Add skill: aibast_payment-plan
11. Add skill: aibast_usage-analysis
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass UTILITY_BILLING_ASSISTANCE-01: Customer Service Representative
15. Pass UTILITY_BILLING_ASSISTANCE-02: Billing Specialist
16. Pass UTILITY_BILLING_ASSISTANCE-03: Revenue Services Supervisor
17. Pass UTILITY_BILLING_ASSISTANCE-04: Assistance Coordinator
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: UTILITY_BILLING_ASSISTANCE-01, UTILITY_BILLING_ASSISTANCE-02, UTILITY_BILLING_ASSISTANCE-03, UTILITY_BILLING_ASSISTANCE-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, its smoke test calls `UtilityBillingAssistanceAgent` and returns the required markers.
- [ ] If built manually, the Draft has the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Unchanged locked persona prompts pass, each in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Each case passes on its final response; a frame without a positive anchor is not proof.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing resident, meter or assistance data. Request only the read scopes the approved utility sources need. Restrict the staff audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Utility billing and customer information system

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Utility data and connection owners

1. **Bind Utility billing and customer information system — read:** Bind approved read-only connector or API actions for account records.

2. **Identity for Utility billing and customer information system:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Utility billing and customer information system:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Utility billing and customer information system:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 6](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): State that the identifier is absent; do not substitute another account. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Say so and return no substituted account.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Advanced metering infrastructure

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Utility data and connection owners

1. **Bind Advanced metering infrastructure — read:** Expose read-only meter-history lookups through a custom connector.

2. **Identity for Advanced metering infrastructure:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Advanced metering infrastructure:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Advanced metering infrastructure:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Diagnose nothing and schedule no repair; describe the anomaly as a screening flag. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim an adjustment, plan, enrollment or notice succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Assistance case-management system

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Utility data and connection owners

1. **Bind Assistance case-management system — read:** Bind approved read-only case actions with record-scoped access.

2. **Identity for Assistance case-management system:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Assistance case-management system:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Assistance case-management system:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Enroll no one; give a preliminary screen and state that no eligibility determination was made. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim an adjustment, plan, enrollment or notice succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Approved payment-plan and repair workflows

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Utility data and connection owners

1. **Bind Approved payment-plan and repair workflows — write:** Keep unavailable until an approval workflow with audit logging passes review (preview).

2. **Identity for Approved payment-plan and repair workflows:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved payment-plan and repair workflows:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved payment-plan and repair workflows:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Create no arrangement; list the options and state that no payment arrangement was created. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return analysis or a draft and name the authorized staff; perform no write.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Outlook and Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Utility data and connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Outlook and Teams — write:** Gate any notice or message workflow behind staff approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Outlook and Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Outlook and Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Outlook and Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Send nothing; responses are internal decision support. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim an adjustment, plan, enrollment or notice succeeded.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Utility data and connection owners

Replace synthetic dictionaries with least-privilege read connectors through dedicated connection references.

### Step 3-7. Write controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Authorized utility staff

Before any write, require authenticated tools, authorization checks, explicit human approval and an audit log.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved billing, metering and case-management connections replace the synthetic inputs and preserve the reviewed input and output contract.
- [ ] Any write tool is separate from analysis, confirmed by an authorized role, validates current state and appends an immutable audit event.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as each staff persona and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic balances, trend bands and screening limits are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked utility corpus | Every locked persona case returns all of its required markers. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| No-write boundary | Any bill adjustment, eligibility decision, enrollment, payment plan, repair, resident notice or account change is no-go. |
| Visual evidence | Require a visible positive anchor without a blocker; reshoot-required frames stay withheld. |
| Release state | The manual and pilot agents are Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Utility service business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Utility service business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Production publication has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved staff audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review resident-service sessions, failed interactions, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses an eligible environment type and a supported restore target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
